before_repeating: current membership for these people and the per-item ledger under this key — or none, where the provider's add is idempotent and the repeat works by the contact pinned on the failure.

input_schema.title: list_membership.add input
input_schema.description: One person, one list, one key. The list is the provider's own: Jason has no list entity, so the planner names it.

channel.description: Which of the contact's channels this operation consumes. Exactly that one channel is projected into `contacts[0].channels`.

contacts.description: This version addresses one person per work item, in the collection shape the level-1 contract uses.

idempotency_key.description: The work item's own identifier: stable across every attempt, which is what makes a ledger under this key answerable.

channels.description: Only the channel the operation consumes, never the person's whole reachability.

items.description: One outcome per person, with the reason. A partial success reported as a single verdict is a defect.

contact.description: The provider's identifier for the contact this call ensured, pinned so no later call has to match the person by address again.

recovery_read.reads: The membership of the pinned contact in the list named by `args.list.external_id`, and the ledger entry under this idempotency key. Where the provider's add is idempotent (a second add of the same contact leaves one membership), a repeat worked by the contact pinned on the failure needs no read; with no pin learned, the contact the first attempt may have made is found by a read first, never created again from the person's fields.
recovery_read.justification: A duplicate add is harmless at most providers, but the contact creation it implies may be metered, and a second contact is a merge nobody asked for. Consumption pricing is the general case: a repeat after a crash is a real charge, not a wasted round trip. Whichever way a repeat goes, it works by the contact the failure pinned, or by the one a read finds first, so it never creates a second one.

failure_codes.when: The identifier pinned for this person no longer resolves at the provider, so the operation cannot act on the person it was told to act on. Working by the pinned identifier is the rule, so this is reported rather than re-matched by address.
More than one provider contact carries this address, so picking one would be guessing and nothing was done. A person resolves the duplicate at the provider, then proposes the work again.
The provider holds no list under `args.list.external_id`.
The provider's own suppression register holds this address, so it must not be added to an outreach list.
The provider will not accept the channel value for the channel named, so no later attempt can accept it either.
The account will not hold another contact, or another member of this list.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, or the plugin could not finish a lookup it needs, so nothing the operation asks for was done. Repeating it runs the same call again.
The plugin's own credential does not let it write lists for this account.
The provider refused the write for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side, before anything was written.

The provider was called and no answer arrived, so the add may already have happened. The next attempt reads before it writes, or repeats an add the provider makes idempotent, worked by the pin or, with none, by the contact a read finds first.

conformance: A contact pinned under `contacts[0].external_ids.contact` is worked by that identifier, and never matched again by the channel value.

A contact with no pin is looked up by the channel value first and created from it only when the provider holds nobody under it; the provider's identifier comes back under `external_ids.contact` either way.

A second call under the same idempotency key performs no second effect. It answers `already_member` where the provider says the person was on the list already, and `added` where the provider's add is idempotent and it cannot tell.

An attempt after a lost answer reads before it writes, or repeats an add the provider makes idempotent, worked by the contact pinned on the failure and, with no pin, by the contact a read finds first, so one crash leaves one effect rather than two.
An address the provider suppresses fails `suppressed` as permanent, rather than being added.
The result carries exactly one item, and its `contact_id` is the identifier the call was given.
